display.text:
# Дизайн: приём заявок (Lead API) с лендинга «Кварта»

Дата: 2026-10-15
Статус: утверждён (вариант A: полные DDD-слои; D1: advisory-лок Postgres)

## 1. Контекст и цель

Лендинг кофейной мастерской «Кварта» (макет `VitaiWorldTest` в Figma,
десктоп + мобильная версия) присылает заявки на бэкенд. Нужен публичный
эндпоинт приёма заявок и товарная модель каталога, чтобы:

- посетитель оставил имя, телефон, интерес (подписка / разовый заказ /
  вопрос), необязательно выбрал кофе и написал комментарий;
- белорусский номер проверялся, а при ошибке человек видел понятную
  подсказку (текст из макета);
- повторная отправка того же номера в течение 10 минут (включая двойной
  клик) не создавала вторую заявку;
- менеджер в `/admin` видел заявку, её статус и источник: из какой
  рекламы, с какого объявления, с какой страницы;
- источник сохранялся целиком, отсутствующие поля — `null`;
- при неудачной отправке фронт мог показать понятное человеку сообщение.

Задача — только бэкенд. Форма в `frontend/` (Next.js) — отдельная задача;
контракт и тексты ошибок для неё описаны здесь.

## 2. Что взято из макета `VitaiWorldTest`

Файл Figma `VitaiWorldTest`, страница «Page 1»: фреймы «Кварта —
десктопный сайт» (`210:2`) и «Кварта — мобильный сайт» (`210:222`).

Разбор релевантных узлов:

- **Форма** (`210:183`, мобильная `210:398`, ошибка `210:494`):
  - radio «Как хотите заказывать?»: «Подписка» (`210:194`), «Разовый
    заказ» (`210:198`);
  - «Ваше имя», плейсхолдер «Как к вам обращаться»;
  - «Телефон», плейсхолдер `+375 (__) ___-__-__`;
  - селект «Какой кофе? Необязательно», плейсхолдер «Помогите выбрать»;
  - кнопка «Оставить заявку»; подпись «Менеджер перезвонит…»;
  - состояние ошибки: под полем телефона красный текст «Пожалуйста,
    введите корректный номер телефона» (`210:527`).
- **Каталог** (`210:76`): 4 позиции с кодом происхождения (BR/CO/ET/DR),
  вкусовыми нотами, описанием, способом приготовления и двумя вариантами
  фасовки с ценами в BYN (250 Г / 500 Г; 10 шт / 20 шт).
- **Подписка** (`210:139`): «Набор Кварты», 2 × 250 г каждую неделю,
  48 BYN за набор.
- Контакты: Минск, ул. Короля, 9; доставка по пятницам от 50 BYN.

Расхождения ТЗ и макета (решения согласованы с заказчиком):

1. В макете 2 варианта интереса, в ТЗ — 3 (включая «вопрос»). В API/БД
   закладываем 3 значения; третий radio дорисует фронт.
2. «Комментарий» из ТЗ и селект «Какой кофе?» из макета — разные поля:
   селект пишется в `product_id` (FK), комментарий — отдельное
   необязательное текстовое поле.
3. «credentials» из списка полей = имя клиента, колонка `name`.

## 3. Архитектура

### 3.1. Слои

Вариант A — полные DDD-слои, как заявлено в AGENTS.md
(`domain — модели и исключения`):

- `domain` — сущности-датаклассы и enum'ы (`Lead`, `LeadSource`,
  `Product`, `ProductVariant`, `Interest`, `ProductKind`), без внешних
  зависимостей; плюс доменные исключения (расширение существующего
  `domain/exceptions.py`).
- `application` — use case'ы `CreateLead`, `ListProducts` и порты-Protocol
  для репозиториев; логика дедупликации (окно) описана здесь.
- `infrastructure` — SQLAlchemy-модели, репозитории (advisory-лок +
  окно + INSERT в одной транзакции), адаптер нормализации телефона
  (`phonenumbers`).
- `presentation` — pydantic-схемы, роутеры `/api/v1`, зависимости,
  sqladmin ModelView'ы; здесь же сборка (composition root — `main.py`,
  `dependencies.py`).

Нормализация телефона живёт в `infrastructure/phone.py` (внешняя
библиотека `phonenumbers` не попадает в `domain`/`application`); схема
запроса вызывает её из валидатора поля — это осознанный composition-шов
на границе API.

### 3.2. Дерево файлов

```
backend/
├── src/app/
│   ├── domain/
│   │   ├── exceptions.py          # + ValidationError (422, validation_error)
│   │   ├── leads.py               # Interest, Lead, LeadSource
│   │   └── products.py            # ProductKind, Product, ProductVariant
│   ├── application/
│   │   ├── leads/
│   │   │   └── create_lead.py     # CreateLead, CreateLeadResult
│   │   ├── products/
│   │   │   └── list_products.py   # ListProducts
│   │   └── ports/
│   │       ├── lead_repository.py     # Protocol
│   │       └── product_repository.py  # Protocol
│   ├── infrastructure/
│   │   ├── phone.py               # normalize_belarus_phone(raw) -> E.164
│   │   └── db/
│   │       ├── base.py            # (существует, не меняется)
│   │       ├── models/
│   │       │   ├── __init__.py    # импорт Order/Product/ProductVariant
│   │       │   ├── order.py
│   │       │   └── product.py
│   │       └── repositories/
│   │           ├── lead_repository.py
│   │           └── product_repository.py
│   └── presentation/
│       ├── dependencies.py        # + get_create_lead, get_list_products
│       ├── main.py                # + add_view, + роутеры (изменяется)
│       ├── admin/
│       │   ├── orders.py          # OrderAdmin
│       │   └── products.py        # ProductAdmin (inline-варианты)
│       └── api/v1/
│           ├── __init__.py        # подключение leads/products роутеров
│           ├── leads.py
│           ├── products.py
│           └── schemas.py
├── alembic/
│   ├── env.py                     # + импорт моделей для autogenerate
│   └── versions/
│       ├── <revA>_products_and_orders.py
│       └── <revB>_seed_products.py
├── tests/
│   ├── conftest.py                # + LEAD_DEDUP_WINDOW_MINUTES в ENV_NAMES
│   ├── domain/test_leads.py, test_products.py, test_exceptions.py (+)
│   ├── application/test_create_lead.py, test_list_products.py
│   ├── infrastructure/test_phone.py, test_models.py
│   │   └── test_lead_repository.py, test_product_repository.py (маппинг)
│   ├── admin/test_views.py
│   └── api/
│       ├── test_leads.py
│       └── test_products.py
├── pyproject.toml / poetry.lock   # + phonenumbers
└── .env.example                   # + LEAD_DEDUP_WINDOW_MINUTES
```

## 4. Модель данных

Идентификаторы — `bigint` identity; именование ограничений — из
существующего `NAMING_CONVENTION` (`infrastructure/db/base.py`). Enum'ы
хранятся как `varchar` + `CHECK` (без PG-enum: проще миграции).
Все временные метки — `timestamptz`, `created_at`/`updated_at` с
`server_default now()`, `updated_at` обновляется на уровне SQLAlchemy.

### 4.1. `products`

| Колонка | Тип | Правила |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | bigint | PK |
| `code` | varchar(8) | not null, unique (BR/CO/ET/DR/SET) |
| `name` | varchar(200) | not null |
| `kind` | varchar(20) | not null, CHECK: `beans` \| `assorted` \| `set` |
| `tasting_notes` | varchar(300) | null (ноты вкуса) |
| `description` | text | null |
| `brew_method` | varchar(300) | null (для чего подходит) |
| `is_active` | boolean | not null, default true |
| `sort_order` | integer | not null, default 0 |
| `created_at` / `updated_at` | timestamptz | not null |

### 4.2. `product_variants` (фасовка и цена)

| Колонка | Тип | Правила |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | bigint | PK |
| `product_id` | bigint | FK → `products.id` ON DELETE CASCADE, not null |
| `packaging_label` | varchar(50) | not null («250 Г», «10 шт», «2 × 250 г») |
| `price` | numeric(10,2) | not null, CHECK ≥ 0; валюта BYN |
| `weight_grams` | integer | null, CHECK ≥ 0 |
| `units` | integer | null, CHECK ≥ 0 (для дрипов: 10/20 шт) |
| `is_active` | boolean | not null, default true |
| `sort_order` | integer | not null, default 0 |
| `created_at` / `updated_at` | timestamptz | not null |

Ограничение: `unique (product_id, packaging_label)`.

### 4.3. `orders` (заявка)

| Колонка | Тип | Правила |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | bigint | PK |
| `name` | varchar(200) | not null (имя клиента) |
| `interest` | varchar(20) | not null, CHECK: `subscription` \| `one_time` \| `question` |
| `phone_number` | varchar(20) | not null, E.164 (+375XXXXXXXXX) |
| `product_id` | bigint | FK → `products.id` ON DELETE SET NULL, null |
| `comment` | text | null, ≤ 2000 символов (валидация приложения) |
| `is_handled` | boolean | not null, default false |
| `utm_source` | varchar(255) | null |
| `utm_medium` | varchar(255) | null |
| `utm_campaign` | varchar(255) | null |
| `utm_content` | varchar(255) | null |
| `utm_term` | varchar(255) | null |
| `referrer` | varchar(1024) | null |
| `page_url` | varchar(1024) | null |
| `source_extra` | jsonb | null (все прочие присланные параметры) |
| `created_at` / `updated_at` | timestamptz | not null |

Индексы: `(phone_number, created_at)` — для дедупликации;
`created_at` — для списка в админке. `is_handled` отдельного индекса не
получает (низкая кардинальность; фильтр по нему — по остаточному
принципу).

### 4.4. Сид из макета (data-миграция)

| code | name | kind | варианты (label, price, weight/units) |
|---|---|---|---|
| BR | Бразилия Серрадо | beans | 250 Г — 26.00 (250); 500 Г — 52.00 (500) |
| CO | Колумбия Уила | beans | 250 Г — 29.00 (250); 500 Г — 58.00 (500) |
| ET | Эфиопия Иргачеффе | beans | 250 Г — 32.00 (250); 500 Г — 64.00 (500) |
| DR | Дрип-пакеты «Кварта» (Ассорти) | assorted | 10 шт — 18.00 (10); 20 шт — 36.00 (20) |

регистром: BR «Шоколад · орех · карамель» / «Плотный и спокойный.
Понятный кофе на каждый день.» / «Для эспрессо, турки и молочных
напитков»; CO «Красное яблоко · какао · тростниковый сахар» / «Сочный,
но без резкости. Когда хочется чуть ярче.» / «Для фильтра и эспрессо»;
ET «Бергамот · цитрус · цветочный мёд» / «Лёгкий и ароматный. Хорош без
молока.» / «Для воронки, фильтра и аэропресса»; DR — описание «10
порционных пакетиков. Внутри — Бразилия, Колумбия и Эфиопия. Идеально
для офиса и поездок. Просто добавь горячую воду.», ноты «Кофе в дорогу ·
для офиса»; SET — описание про подписку, ноты «2 × 250 г каждую
неделю». `sort_order` — 1..5 в порядке таблицы.

### 4.5. Миграции

Две ревизии (обе с `down_revision` от текущего head `4d28216bc024`):

1. Схема: три таблицы, ограничения, индексы.
2. Данные: сид 5 товаров с вариантами (downgrade — удаление по `code`).

`alembic/env.py` дополняется импортом моделей (иначе autogenerate их не
видит). Offline-проверка `alembic upgrade head --sql` — обязательна.

## 5. API

### 5.1. `POST /api/v1/lead`

`Content-Type: application/json`. Тело:

```json
{
  "name": "Иван",
  "phone_number": "+375 (29) 123-45-67",
  "interest": "subscription",
  "product_id": 3,
  "comment": "Хочу на четверг",
  "source": {
    "utm_source": "yandex",
    "utm_medium": "cpc",
    "utm_campaign": "coffee_minsk",
    "utm_content": "ad_32",
    "utm_term": "кофе с доставкой",
    "referrer": "https://yandex.by/...",
    "page_url": "https://kvarta.by/",
    "gclid": "CjcK..."
  }
}
```

Правила полей:

- `name` — строка, trim, 1..200 символов, обязательна.
- `phone_number` — строка 1..32, любой формат (+375…, 375…, 80…
  национальный, со скобками/дефисами/пробелами); нормализуется в E.164.
- `interest` — `subscription` | `one_time` | `question`, обязательно.
- `product_id` — целое или null; товар должен существовать и быть
  активным.
- `comment` — строка ≤ 2000 или null.
- `source` — объект `str -> str` или null. Известные ключи
  (`utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, `utm_content`, `utm_term`,
  `referrer`, `page_url`) пишутся в одноимённые колонки, все прочие — в
  `source_extra` (jsonb). Пустые строки нормализуются в `null`. Значения
  длиннее 1024 символов обрезаются с предупреждением в лог (заявку не
  роняем — «сохранять всё, что пришло» best-effort).

Ответы:

- **201** `{"id": 42, "duplicate": false}` — заявка создана.
- **200** `{"id": 41, "duplicate": true}` — повтор номера в окне
  дедупликации; вторая заявка не создаётся, существующая не изменяется.
- **422** — конверт ошибок (см. 5.3).
- **500** — конверт `internal_error` (`details` только вне production).

### 5.2. `GET /api/v1/products`

Публичный список активных товаров с активными вариантами, сортировка по
`sort_order`, затем `id`. Цены — строки с 2 знаками (Pydantic сериализует
`Decimal` строкой), валюта BYN:

```json
[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "code": "BR",
    "name": "Бразилия Серрадо",
    "kind": "beans",
    "tasting_notes": "Шоколад · орех · карамель",
    "description": "Плотный и спокойный. Понятный кофе на каждый день.",
    "brew_method": "Для эспрессо, турки и молочных напитков",
    "variants": [
      {"id": 1, "packaging_label": "250 Г", "price": "26.00",
       "weight_grams": 250, "units": null}
    ]
  }
]
```

### 5.3. Ошибки и тексты для человека

Используется существующий конверт
`{"error": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "details": ...}}`
(`presentation/errors.py`, не меняется).

- Невалидный телефон → 422, `details[]` =
  `{"type": "phone_invalid", "loc": ["body", "phone_number"],
  "msg": "Пожалуйста, введите корректный номер телефона", ...}` —
  текст из макета, задаётся через `PydanticCustomError` в валидаторе
  (без английского префикса «Value error»).
- Неактивный/несуществующий `product_id` → 422,
  `code = validation_error`, message «Выбранный кофе больше недоступен —
  выберите другой или оставьте поле пустым» (доменная `ValidationError`
  из `domain/exceptions.py` со `status_code = 422`).
- Прочие ошибки полей (имя, интерес, длина) — стандартный 422;
  `details[].loc` и `details[].type` дают фронту всё для локальных
  текстов.
- Фронт показывает: `details[].msg` под соответствующим полем; на
  дубль — «Заявка уже отправлена — менеджер перезвонит»; на 5xx/сетевую
  ошибку — «Не удалось отправить заявку. Попробуйте ещё раз или
  позвоните нам.»

### 5.4. Дедупликация

- Окно — `LEAD_DEDUP_WINDOW_MINUTES` (default 10, см. раздел 9).
- Ключ — нормализованный E.164: разные записи одного номера
  (`+375 (29)…`, `8029…`) дедуплицируются между собой.
- Сравнивается только номер; остальные поля не важны (per ТЗ).
- Реализация (D1) — в одной транзакции репозитория
  `add_if_not_recent(lead, window)`:

  ```sql
  SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(:phone, 0));
  -- SELECT существующей заявки:
  --   WHERE phone_number = :phone
  --     AND created_at >= now() - make_interval(mins => :window)
  --   ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1
  -- если нет — INSERT ... RETURNING id
  ```

  Advisory-лок сериализует одновременные запросы по одному номеру, что
  закрывает двойной клик и работу нескольких воркеров gunicorn; при
  отсутствии гонки лок бесплатен.

## 6. Источник заявки (ad-source)

- Канал — объект `source` в теле POST: фронт при загрузке страницы
  собирает UTM/`page_url`/`referrer` из URL и передаёт заявкой
  (рекламные параметры не теряются при переходах по сайту).
- Известные ключи → колонки `utm_*`, `referrer`, `page_url`;
  произвольные → `source_extra` (jsonb). Ничего не отбрасывается,
  отсутствующее — `null` (в т.ч. когда `source` не пришёл вовсе).
- Менеджер видит «из какой рекламы» (`utm_source`/`utm_medium`), «с
  какого объявления» (`utm_content`/`utm_term`), «с какой страницы»
  (`page_url`) в списке заявок `/admin`.

## 7. Телефон

- Библиотека `phonenumbers` (Google libphonenumber), регион BY.
- Принимаются форматы: `+375 29 123-45-67`, `375291234567`, `80 29
  1234567`, `(029) 1234567` и т.п.; городские номера (17) — валидны.
- Проверка: номер парсится и валиден для региона BY; иначе — 422 с
  текстом из макета (см. 5.3).
- Хранение — E.164 (`+375291234567`) в `orders.phone_number`.
- `phonenumbers` — чистая python-библиотека, капов `requires-python`/
  aiogram не затрагивает. Для mypy: если пакет без `py.typed` — стабы
  `types-phonenumbers` (dev) или override `ignore_missing_imports` как
  для `sqladmin.*`.

## 8. Админка (sqladmin)

`Admin(...)` в `main.py` сохраняется в переменную, регистрируются view:

- `OrderAdmin`: список — `created_at`, `name`, `phone_number`,
  `interest`, `product_id`, `utm_source`, `utm_content`, `page_url`,
  `is_handled`; поиск по имени/телефону; фильтры — `is_handled`,
  `interest`, `utm_source`, диапазон дат; `can_create = false`,
  `can_delete = false`; редактируется только `is_handled` (менеджер
  отмечает обработку, данные заявки не переписываются).
- `ProductAdmin`: CRUD товаров; список — `code`, `name`, `kind`,
  `is_active`, `sort_order`.
- `ProductVariantAdmin`: CRUD вариантов фасовки/цен с фильтром по товару
  (ядро sqladmin 0.32 не поддерживает inline-модели — проверено по
  API-референсу, поэтому варианты ведутся отдельным view).

## 9. Настройки

Новая переменная (в `Settings`, `.env.example` и `ENV_NAMES` тестов):

| Переменная | Пример | Смысл |
|---|---|---|
| `LEAD_DEDUP_WINDOW_MINUTES` | `10` | окно дедупликации заявок по номеру, минуты; pydantic-ограничение 1..1440, default 10 |

## 10. Тесты (без реальной БД)

По существующим паттернам: фейки/`dependency_overrides`, httpx
`ASGITransport`, `asyncio_mode = "auto"`, никаких подключений к Postgres.

- `tests/domain/test_leads.py` — значения и поведение enum'ов/сущностей.
- `tests/application/test_create_lead.py` — фейковые репозитории:
  создание; дубль в окне → `duplicate=True`, без второго INSERT;
  неактивный/неизвестный товар → `ValidationError`; `source`/`comment`
  null.
- `tests/infrastructure/test_phone.py` — нормализация форматов
  (`+375…`, `375…`, `80…`, со скобками); мусор и зарубежные номера →
  `ValueError`.
- `tests/api/test_leads.py` — 201; 200 + `duplicate=true`; 422 на битый
  телефон с текстом из макета (`loc=["body","phone_number"]`);
  422 на пустое имя; передача source/comment в use case (через
  override-фейк); конверт ошибок.
- `tests/api/test_products.py` — 200, состав и сортировка, цены
  строками, отсев неактивных.
- `tests/infrastructure/test_models.py` — имена таблиц, индексов и
  уникальных ограничений в metadata (без БД).
- `tests/infrastructure/test_lead_repository.py` и
  `test_product_repository.py` — маппинг ORM → domain (без БД).
- `tests/admin/test_views.py` — списки
  `/admin/{order,product,product-variant}/list` требуют логина (302),
  т.е. view зарегистрированы.
- SQL-код репозиториев в CI не исполняется (нет БД) — покрывается
  offline-проверкой миграций и smoke-прогоном в docker compose
  (раздел 12).

## 11. Инструменты качества

Без изменений конфигурации: ruff (`py314`, line-length 100), mypy
(strict, `disallow_untyped_defs`), pytest. `alembic/versions` остаётся
исключённым из ruff/mypy.

## 12. Верификация (обязательно)

1. `poetry install` (добавляется `phonenumbers`).
2. `poetry run mypy src tests`
3. `poetry run ruff check .` и `poetry run ruff format --check .`
4. `poetry run pytest -q`
5. `poetry run alembic upgrade head --sql` — offline-проверка обеих
   миграций.
6. Smoke в docker compose (`docker compose up -d --build`; применить
   миграции сервисом `migrate`):
   - `POST /api/v1/lead` валидной заявкой → 201, `duplicate=false`;
   - повтор той же заявки сразу → 200, `duplicate=true`, в БД одна
     строка;
   - `POST` с телефоном «+375 29» → 422, `msg` = «Пожалуйста, введите
     корректный номер телефона»;
   - `GET /api/v1/products` → 5 товаров из сида с вариантами;
   - `/admin` — заявка видна, источник отображается, `is_handled`
     переключается.
7. `git status` / `git diff` — не затронуты Dockerfile, compose.yaml,
   .pre-commit-config.yaml, frontend.

## 13. Вне границ задачи (не делаем)

- Форма и показ ошибок во `frontend/` (Next.js) — контракт описан,
  реализация отдельной задачей.
- Rate limiting, CAPTCHA, анти-спам сверх дедупликации.
- Уведомления менеджеру (telegram/email), aiogram-код.
- Статусы заявки сверх `is_handled`, история изменений.
- Оплата, корзина, остатки, картинки товаров, цены в других валютах.
- Публичные ссылки/UUID-идентификаторы, API-auth для чтения заявок.
- Изменения Dockerfile, compose.yaml, .pre-commit-config.yaml, фронтенда.

## 14. Процесс реализации

1. Эта спека (файл в `docs/`, каталог в корневом `.gitignore` — в git
   не коммитится).
2. Implementation plan (writing-plans).
3. SDD: ветка `feat/lead-api`; задачи с коммитами (`feat(backend): …`)
   и независимым ревью каждой задачи; финальное ревью всей ветки.
4. Финальная верификация по разделу 12; ветку не мержить без явной
   команды заказчика.

import logging
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator
from pydantic_core import PydanticCustomError

from app.domain.leads import Interest, Lead, LeadSource
from app.domain.products import ProductKind
from app.infrastructure.phone import normalize_belarus_phone

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

PHONE_INVALID_MESSAGE = "Пожалуйста, введите корректный номер телефона"
SOURCE_INVALID_MESSAGE = "Некорректный параметр источника"
MAX_SOURCE_VALUE_LENGTH = 1024
KNOWN_SOURCE_KEYS = frozenset(
    {"utm_source", "utm_medium", "utm_campaign", "utm_content", "utm_term", "referrer", "page_url"}
)


class LeadCreateRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)

    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)
    phone_number: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=32)
    interest: Interest
    product_id: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=1)
    comment: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=2000)
    source: dict[str, str] | None = None

    @field_validator("phone_number")
    @classmethod
    def _normalize_phone(cls, value: str) -> str:
        try:
            return normalize_belarus_phone(value)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise PydanticCustomError("phone_invalid", PHONE_INVALID_MESSAGE) from exc

    @field_validator("source", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _clean_source(cls, value: Any) -> Any:
        if value is None:
            return None
        if not isinstance(value, dict):
            raise PydanticCustomError("source_invalid", SOURCE_INVALID_MESSAGE)
        cleaned: dict[str, str] = {}
        for key, raw in value.items():
            if not isinstance(key, str) or not isinstance(raw, str):
                raise PydanticCustomError("source_invalid", SOURCE_INVALID_MESSAGE)
            stripped = raw.strip()
            if not stripped:
                continue
            if len(stripped) > MAX_SOURCE_VALUE_LENGTH:
                logger.warning(
                    "Source value for %r truncated to %d chars", key, MAX_SOURCE_VALUE_LENGTH
                )
                stripped = stripped[:MAX_SOURCE_VALUE_LENGTH]
            cleaned[key] = stripped
        return cleaned

    def to_lead(self) -> Lead:
        return Lead(
            name=self.name,
            phone_number=self.phone_number,
            interest=self.interest,
            product_id=self.product_id,
            comment=self.comment,
            source=to_domain_source(self.source),
        )


def to_domain_source(raw: dict[str, str] | None) -> LeadSource | None:
    if raw is None:
        return None
    extra = {key: value for key, value in raw.items() if key not in KNOWN_SOURCE_KEYS}
    return LeadSource(
        utm_source=raw.get("utm_source"),
        utm_medium=raw.get("utm_medium"),
        utm_campaign=raw.get("utm_campaign"),
        utm_content=raw.get("utm_content"),
        utm_term=raw.get("utm_term"),
        referrer=raw.get("referrer"),
        page_url=raw.get("page_url"),
        extra=extra,
    )


class LeadCreateResponse(BaseModel):
    id: int
    duplicate: bool


class ProductVariantOut(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

    id: int
    packaging_label: str
    price: Decimal
    weight_grams: int | None
    units: int | None


class ProductOut(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

    id: int
    code: str
    name: str
    kind: ProductKind
    tasting_notes: str | None
    description: str | None
    brew_method: str | None
    variants: list[ProductVariantOut]
```

async def get_session(request: Request) -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
    sessionmaker = request.app.state.sessionmaker
    async with sessionmaker() as session:
        yield session


def get_readiness_check(request: Request) -> CheckReadiness:
    return CheckReadiness(AsyncDatabaseProbe(request.app.state.db_engine))


def get_create_lead(request: Request) -> CreateLead:
    sessionmaker = request.app.state.sessionmaker
    return CreateLead(
        leads=SqlAlchemyLeadRepository(sessionmaker),
        products=SqlAlchemyProductRepository(sessionmaker),
        window=timedelta(minutes=request.app.state.settings.lead_dedup_window_minutes),
    )


def get_list_products(request: Request) -> ListProducts:
    return ListProducts(SqlAlchemyProductRepository(request.app.state.sessionmaker))

1: # Task Reviewer Prompt Template
2: 
3: Use this template when dispatching a task reviewer subagent. The reviewer
4: reads the task's diff once and returns two verdicts: spec compliance and
5: code quality.
6: 
7: **Purpose:** Verify one task's implementation matches its requirements (nothing
8: more, nothing less) and is well-built (clean, tested, maintainable)
9: 
10: ```
11: Subagent (general-purpose):
12:   description: "Review Task N (spec + quality)"
13:   model: [MODEL — REQUIRED: choose per SKILL.md Model Selection; an omitted
14:          model silently inherits the session's most expensive one]
15:   prompt: |
16:     You are reviewing one task's implementation: first whether it matches its
17:     requirements, then whether it is well-built. This is a task-scoped gate,
18:     not a merge review — a broad whole-branch review happens separately after
19:     all tasks are complete.
20: 
21:     ## What Was Requested
22: 
23:     Read the task brief: [BRIEF_FILE]
24: 
25:     Global constraints from the spec/design that bind this task:
26:     [GLOBAL_CONSTRAINTS]
27: 
28:     ## What the Implementer Claims They Built
29: 
30:     Read the implementer's report: [REPORT_FILE]
31: 
32:     ## Diff Under Review
33: 
34:     **Base:** [BASE_SHA]
35:     **Head:** [HEAD_SHA]
36:     **Diff file:** [DIFF_FILE]
37: 
38:     Read the diff file once — it contains the commit list, a stat summary,
39:     and the full diff with surrounding context, and it is your view of the
40:     change. The diff's context lines ARE the changed files: do not Read a
41:     changed file separately unless a hunk you must judge is cut off
42:     mid-function — and say so in your report. Do not re-run git commands.
43:     If the diff file is missing, fetch the diff yourself:
44:     `git diff --stat [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]` and `git diff [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]`.
45:     Do not crawl the broader codebase. Inspect code outside the diff only
46:     to evaluate a concrete risk you can name — one focused check per named
47:     risk, and name both the risk and what you checked in your report.
48:     Cross-cutting changes are legitimate named risks: if the diff changes
49:     lock ordering, a function or API contract, or shared mutable state,
50:     checking the call sites is the right method.
51: 
52:     Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working
53:     tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way.
54: 
55:     ## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents
56: 
57:     Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent to review part
58:     of the diff, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion.
59:     This process already provides every review seat the work gets; a
60:     reviewer you spawn duplicates one of them at full cost, and its
61:     verdict counts for nothing. If the diff feels too large for one
62:     pass, review it in passes yourself and say so in your report.
63: 
64:     ## Do Not Trust the Report
65: 
66:     Treat the implementer's report as unverified claims about the code. It
67:     may be incomplete, inaccurate, or optimistic. Verify the claims against
68:     the diff. Design rationales in the report are claims too: "left it per
69:     YAGNI," "kept it simple deliberately," or any other justification is the
70:     implementer grading their own work. Judge the code on its merits — a
71:     stated rationale never downgrades a finding's severity.
72: 
73:     ## Tests
74: 
75:     The implementer already ran the tests and reported results with TDD
76:     evidence for exactly this code. Do not re-run the suite to confirm their
77:     report. Run a test only when reading the code raises a specific doubt
78:     that no existing run answers — and then a focused test, never a
79:     package-wide suite, race detector run, or repeated/high-count loop. If
80:     heavy validation seems warranted, recommend it in your report instead of
81:     running it. If you cannot run commands in this environment, name the
82:     test you would run.
83: 
84:     Warnings or other noise in the implementer's reported test output are
85:     findings — test output should be pristine.
86: 
87:     Evidence you cannot see is not evidence that doesn't exist. If the
88:     report or its test evidence looks truncated, or you cannot locate the
89:     results it claims, re-read the file at its stated path — and if it is
90:     genuinely missing or garbled, report that as a gap for the controller.
91:     Re-running the suite to regenerate what you failed to read is not
92:     verification; illegibility of the evidence is not invalidation of it.
93: 
94:     ## Part 1: Spec Compliance
95: 
96:     Compare the diff against What Was Requested:
97: 
98:     - **Missing:** requirements they skipped, missed, or claimed without
99:       implementing
100:     - **Extra:** features that weren't requested, over-engineering, unneeded
101:       "nice to haves"
102:     - **Misunderstood:** right feature built the wrong way, wrong problem
103:       solved
104: 
105:     If the brief lists several files each with its own change (a batched
106:     dispatch), check the diff against that list file by file: every listed
107:     file must have its corresponding hunk. A listed file the diff never
108:     touches is a Missing finding, no matter how clean the rest of the
109:     batch looks.

111:     If a requirement cannot be verified from this diff alone (it lives in
112:     unchanged code or spans tasks), report it as a ⚠️ item instead of
113:     broadening your search.

118:     - Clean separation of concerns?
119:     - Proper error handling?
120:     - DRY without premature abstraction?
121:     - Edge cases handled?
122: 
123:     **Tests:**

125:     - Are the task's edge cases covered?
126: 
127:     **Structure:**

display.text:
# Task Reviewer Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching a task reviewer subagent. The reviewer
reads the task's diff once and returns two verdicts: spec compliance and
code quality.

**Purpose:** Verify one task's implementation matches its requirements (nothing
more, nothing less) and is well-built (clean, tested, maintainable)

```
Subagent (general-purpose):
  description: "Review Task N (spec + quality)"
  model: [MODEL — REQUIRED: choose per SKILL.md Model Selection; an omitted
         model silently inherits the session's most expensive one]
  prompt: |
    You are reviewing one task's implementation: first whether it matches its
    requirements, then whether it is well-built. This is a task-scoped gate,
    not a merge review — a broad whole-branch review happens separately after
    all tasks are complete.

    ## What Was Requested

    Read the task brief: [BRIEF_FILE]

    Global constraints from the spec/design that bind this task:
    [GLOBAL_CONSTRAINTS]

    ## What the Implementer Claims They Built

    Read the implementer's report: [REPORT_FILE]

    ## Diff Under Review

    **Base:** [BASE_SHA]
    **Head:** [HEAD_SHA]
    **Diff file:** [DIFF_FILE]

    Read the diff file once — it contains the commit list, a stat summary,
    and the full diff with surrounding context, and it is your view of the
    change. The diff's context lines ARE the changed files: do not Read a
    changed file separately unless a hunk you must judge is cut off
    mid-function — and say so in your report. Do not re-run git commands.
    If the diff file is missing, fetch the diff yourself:
    `git diff --stat [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]` and `git diff [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]`.
    Do not crawl the broader codebase. Inspect code outside the diff only
    to evaluate a concrete risk you can name — one focused check per named
    risk, and name both the risk and what you checked in your report.
    Cross-cutting changes are legitimate named risks: if the diff changes
    lock ordering, a function or API contract, or shared mutable state,
    checking the call sites is the right method.

    Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working
    tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way.

    ## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

    Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent to review part
    of the diff, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion.
    This process already provides every review seat the work gets; a
    reviewer you spawn duplicates one of them at full cost, and its
    verdict counts for nothing. If the diff feels too large for one
    pass, review it in passes yourself and say so in your report.

    ## Do Not Trust the Report

    Treat the implementer's report as unverified claims about the code. It
    may be incomplete, inaccurate, or optimistic. Verify the claims against
    the diff. Design rationales in the report are claims too: "left it per
    YAGNI," "kept it simple deliberately," or any other justification is the
    implementer grading their own work. Judge the code on its merits — a
    stated rationale never downgrades a finding's severity.

    ## Tests

    The implementer already ran the tests and reported results with TDD
    evidence for exactly this code. Do not re-run the suite to confirm their
    report. Run a test only when reading the code raises a specific doubt
    that no existing run answers — and then a focused test, never a
    package-wide suite, race detector run, or repeated/high-count loop. If
    heavy validation seems warranted, recommend it in your report instead of
    running it. If you cannot run commands in this environment, name the
    test you would run.

    Warnings or other noise in the implementer's reported test output are
    findings — test output should be pristine.

    Evidence you cannot see is not evidence that doesn't exist. If the
    report or its test evidence looks truncated, or you cannot locate the
    results it claims, re-read the file at its stated path — and if it is
    genuinely missing or garbled, report that as a gap for the controller.
    Re-running the suite to regenerate what you failed to read is not
    verification; illegibility of the evidence is not invalidation of it.

    ## Part 1: Spec Compliance

    Compare the diff against What Was Requested:

    - **Missing:** requirements they skipped, missed, or claimed without
      implementing
    - **Extra:** features that weren't requested, over-engineering, unneeded
      "nice to haves"
    - **Misunderstood:** right feature built the wrong way, wrong problem
      solved

    If the brief lists several files each with its own change (a batched
    dispatch), check the diff against that list file by file: every listed
    file must have its corresponding hunk. A listed file the diff never
    touches is a Missing finding, no matter how clean the rest of the
    batch looks.

    If a requirement cannot be verified from this diff alone (it lives in
    unchanged code or spans tasks), report it as a ⚠️ item instead of
    broadening your search.

    ## Part 2: Code Quality

    **Code quality:**
    - Clean separation of concerns?
    - Proper error handling?
    - DRY without premature abstraction?
    - Edge cases handled?

    **Tests:**
    - Do the new and changed tests verify real behavior, not mocks?
    - Are the task's edge cases covered?

    **Structure:**
    - Does each file have one clear responsibility with a well-defined interface?
    - Are units decomposed so they can be understood and tested independently?
    - Is the implementation following the file structure from the plan?
    - Did this change create new files that are already large, or
      significantly grow existing files? (Don't flag pre-existing file
      sizes — focus on what this change contributed.)

    Your report should point at evidence: file:line references for every
    finding and for any check you would otherwise answer with a bare
    "yes." A tight report that cites lines gives the controller everything
    it needs.

    Your final message is the report itself: begin directly with the
    spec-compliance verdict. Every line is a verdict, a finding with
    file:line, or a check you ran — no preamble, no process narration,
    no closing summary.

    ## Calibration

    Categorize issues by actual severity. Not everything is Critical.
    Important means this task cannot be trusted until it is fixed: incorrect
    or fragile behavior, a missed requirement, or maintainability damage you
    would block a merge over — verbatim duplication of a logic block,
    swallowed errors, tests that assert nothing. "Coverage could be broader"
    and polish suggestions are Minor.
    If the plan or brief explicitly mandates something this rubric calls a
    defect (a test that asserts nothing, verbatim duplication of a logic
    block), that IS a finding — report it as Important, labeled
    plan-mandated. The plan's authorship does not grade its own work; the
    human decides.
    Acknowledge what was done well before listing issues — accurate praise
    helps the implementer trust the rest of the feedback.

    ## Output Format

    ### Spec Compliance

    - ✅ Spec compliant | ❌ Issues found: [what's missing/extra/misunderstood,
      with file:line references]
    - ⚠️ Cannot verify from diff: [requirements you could not verify from the
      diff alone, and what the controller should check — report alongside the
      ✅/❌ verdict for everything you could verify]

    ### Strengths
    [What's well done? Be specific.]

    ### Issues

    #### Critical (Must Fix)
    #### Important (Should Fix)
    #### Minor (Nice to Have)

    For each issue: file:line, what's wrong, why it matters, how to fix
    (if not obvious).

    ### Assessment

    **Task quality:** [Approved | Needs fixes]

    **Reasoning:** [1-2 sentence technical assessment]
```

**Placeholders:**
- `[MODEL]` — REQUIRED: reviewer model per SKILL.md Model Selection
- `[BRIEF_FILE]` — REQUIRED: the task brief file (`scripts/task-brief PLAN N`
  prints the path; same file the implementer worked from)
- `[GLOBAL_CONSTRAINTS]` — the binding requirements copied verbatim from
  the plan's Global Constraints section or the spec: exact values, formats,
  and stated relationships between components (not process rules — those
  are already in this template)
- `[REPORT_FILE]` — REQUIRED: the file the implementer wrote its detailed
  report to
- `[BASE_SHA]` — commit before this task
- `[HEAD_SHA]` — current commit
- `[DIFF_FILE]` — REQUIRED: the path the controller wrote the review
  package to (`scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE BASE HEAD` prints the unique
  path it wrote; the package never enters the controller's context)

**Reviewer returns:** Spec Compliance verdict (✅/❌/⚠️), Strengths, Issues
(Critical/Important/Minor), Task quality verdict

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator

from fastapi import Request
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.application.health.check_readiness import CheckReadiness
from app.infrastructure.db.probe import AsyncDatabaseProbe


async def get_session(request: Request) -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
    sessionmaker = request.app.state.sessionmaker
    async with sessionmaker() as session:
        yield session


def get_readiness_check(request: Request) -> CheckReadiness:
    return CheckReadiness(AsyncDatabaseProbe(request.app.state.db_engine))

## Finding (from the task reviewer)

`tests/admin/test_views.py` cannot evidence its stated requirement. The brief frames the 302-to-login test as proof that the views are registered ("i.e. the views are registered"), but under sqladmin 0.32 the login redirect fires before identity resolution, so the test passes even with zero views registered (you observed this yourself: 3 passed pre-implementation). ## Controller ruling (binding)

The spec's intent (§10: the admin test proves the views are registered) outranks the brief's weaker test design. Strengthen `tests/admin/test_views.py`:

1. KEEP the existing parametrized unauthenticated 302 test as-is.
2. ADD a DB-free authenticated discriminator, mirroring your probe: log in through `/admin/login` using the admin credentials the test settings/env already use (look at how `AdminAuthBackend`/existing auth tests do it — e.g. the settings values in `tests/conftest.py` and the app fixture), then:

<skill_content name="requesting-code-review">
# Skill: requesting-code-review

# Requesting Code Review

Dispatch a code reviewer subagent to catch issues before they cascade. The reviewer gets precisely crafted context for evaluation — never your session's history.

**Core principle:** Review early, review often.

## When to Request Review

**Mandatory:**
- After each task in subagent-driven development
- After completing major feature
- Before merge to main

**Optional but valuable:**
- When stuck (fresh perspective)
- Before refactoring (baseline check)
- After fixing complex bug

## How to Request

**1. Get git SHAs:**
```bash
BASE_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)  # or origin/main
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
```

**2. Dispatch code reviewer subagent:**

Dispatch a `general-purpose` subagent, filling the template at [code-reviewer.md](code-reviewer.md)

**Placeholders:**
- `{DESCRIPTION}` - Brief summary of what you built
- `{PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS}` - What it should do
- `{BASE_SHA}` - Starting commit
- `{HEAD_SHA}` - Ending commit

**3. Act on feedback:**
- Fix Critical issues immediately
- Fix Important issues before proceeding
- Note Minor issues for later
- Push back if reviewer is wrong (with reasoning)

## Example

```
[Just completed Task 2: Add verification function]

You: Let me request code review before proceeding.

BASE_SHA=$(git log --oneline | grep "Task 1" | head -1 | awk '{print $1}')
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

[Dispatch code reviewer subagent]
  DESCRIPTION: Added verifyIndex() and repairIndex() with 4 issue types
  PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: Task 2 from docs/superpowers/plans/deployment-plan.md
  BASE_SHA: a7981ec
  HEAD_SHA: 3df7661

[Subagent returns]:
  Strengths: Clean architecture, real tests
  Issues:
    Important: Missing progress indicators
    Minor: Magic number (100) for reporting interval
  Assessment: Ready to proceed

You: [Fix progress indicators]
[Continue to Task 3]
```

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "I'll just review the diff myself instead of dispatching a reviewer" | You're the coordinator — reviewing the diff inline burns the context window you need to keep driving the work. Dispatch a reviewer subagent: the diff and the evaluation live in its context, and only the findings come back to you. |
| "The reviewer needs my whole session history to understand the change" | Hand it precisely crafted context, never your session's history. That keeps the reviewer on the work product, not your thought process. |

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Skip review because "it's simple"
- Ignore Critical issues
- Proceed with unfixed Important issues
- Argue with valid technical feedback

**If reviewer wrong:**
- Push back with technical reasoning
- Show code/tests that prove it works
- Request clarification

See template at: [code-reviewer.md](code-reviewer.md)

# Code Reviewer Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching a code reviewer subagent.

**Purpose:** Review completed work against requirements and code quality standards before it cascades into more work.

```
Subagent (general-purpose):
  description: "Review code changes"
  prompt: |
    You are a Senior Code Reviewer with expertise in software architecture,
    design patterns, and best practices. Your job is to review completed work
    against its plan or requirements and identify issues before they cascade.

    ## What Was Implemented

    [DESCRIPTION]

    ## Requirements / Plan

    [PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS]

    ## Git Range to Review

    **Base:** [BASE_SHA]
    **Head:** [HEAD_SHA]

    ```bash
    git diff --stat [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]
    git diff [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]
    ```

    ## Read-Only Review

    Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way. Use tools like `git show`, `git diff`, and `git log` to inspect history. If you need a working copy of a different revision, check it out into a separate temporary directory (e.g. `git worktree add /tmp/review-[SHA] [SHA]`) — never move HEAD on this checkout.

    ## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

    Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent to review part
    of the diff, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion.
    This process already provides every review seat the work gets; a
    reviewer you spawn duplicates one of them at full cost, and its
    verdict counts for nothing. If the diff feels too large for one
    pass, review it in passes yourself and say so in your report.

    ## What to Check

    **Plan alignment:**
    - Does the implementation match the plan / requirements?
    - Are deviations justified improvements, or problematic departures?
    - Is all planned functionality present?

    **Code quality:**
    - Clean separation of concerns?
    - Proper error handling?
    - Type safety where applicable?
    - DRY without premature abstraction?
    - Edge cases handled?

    **Architecture:**
    - Sound design decisions?
    - Reasonable scalability and performance?
    - Security concerns?
    - Integrates cleanly with surrounding code?

    **Testing:**
    - Tests verify real behavior, not mocks?
    - Edge cases covered?
    - Integration tests where they matter?
    - All tests passing?

    **Production readiness:**
    - Migration strategy if schema changed?
    - Backward compatibility considered?
    - Documentation complete?
    - No obvious bugs?

    ## Calibration

    Categorize issues by actual severity. Not everything is Critical.
    Acknowledge what was done well before listing issues — accurate praise
    helps the implementer trust the rest of the feedback.

    If you find significant deviations from the plan, flag them specifically
    so the implementer can confirm whether the deviation was intentional.
    If you find issues with the plan itself rather than the implementation,
    say so.

    ## Output Format

    ### Strengths
    [What's well done? Be specific.]

    ### Issues

    #### Critical (Must Fix)
    [Bugs, security issues, data loss risks, broken functionality]

    #### Important (Should Fix)
    [Architecture problems, missing features, poor error handling, test gaps]

    #### Minor (Nice to Have)
    [Code style, optimization opportunities, documentation polish]

    For each issue:
    - File:line reference
    - What's wrong
    - Why it matters
    - How to fix (if not obvious)

    ### Recommendations
    [Improvements for code quality, architecture, or process]

    ### Assessment

    **Ready to merge?** [Yes | No | With fixes]

    **Reasoning:** [1-2 sentence technical assessment]

    ## Critical Rules

    **DO:**
    - Categorize by actual severity
    - Be specific (file:line, not vague)
    - Explain WHY each issue matters
    - Acknowledge strengths
    - Give a clear verdict

    **DON'T:**
    - Say "looks good" without checking
    - Mark nitpicks as Critical
    - Give feedback on code you didn't actually read
    - Be vague ("improve error handling")
    - Avoid giving a clear verdict
```

**Placeholders:**
- `[DESCRIPTION]` — brief summary of what was built
- `[PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS]` — what it should do (plan file path, task text, or requirements)
- `[BASE_SHA]` — starting commit
- `[HEAD_SHA]` — ending commit

**Reviewer returns:** Strengths, Issues (Critical / Important / Minor), Recommendations, Assessment

# Final Branch Review: feat/lead-api (b010b66..264aa08)

I reviewed the full diff, spec, plan, ledger, Task 10 report, and verified the checkout read-only: `pytest -q` (85 passed, no warnings), `mypy src tests` (clean), `ruff check`/`format --check` (clean), alembic offline render (`4d28216bc024:head` → exactly 3 CREATE TABLE, head revision `b2e1d3c45a67`), forbidden-path diff (empty), DB state (5 products / 9 variants / 1 smoke order, seed texts match spec §4.4 verbatim), and one targeted integration probe (below).

### Strengths

- **Spec fidelity is excellent.** Enum values, Russian error texts (phone/product/source), response shapes (201/200/422, `duplicate` flag), seed contents/prices/sort orders, admin view restrictions (`can_create/delete=false`, only `is_handled` editable), and migration chain all match the spec exactly. The confirmation email... er, the contract is faithful down to `loc=["body","phone_number"]` and `type="phone_invalid"`.
- **Layering is clean.** domain has no external imports; application only domain + Protocol ports; infrastructure implements ports; the one sanctioned composition seam (`schemas.py` → `infrastructure.phone`) is exactly what spec §3.1 prescribes. `alembic/env.py` model registration is correct.
- **Dedup design is sound and correctly implemented** (`lead_repository.py:14-46`): advisory xact lock is the first statement, READ COMMITTED guarantees the post-lock SELECT sees the competitor's committed row, indexed by `(phone_number, created_at)`, and the smoke proved 201→200 with exactly one DB row. This is the D1 design executed properly.
- **Full ad-source persistence** with sensible normalization (trim, empty→null, truncate+warn) and `gclid`-style extras in JSONB — verified in DB.
- **Migrations** are chained, offline-verifiable, seed with explicit ids + `setval` (Task 10 verified `last_value=5/9, is_called=t`), and online application through asyncpg was smoke-verified (Watch 1 closed).
- **Task 9's review fix is genuinely better than the brief**: the authenticated 403/404 discriminator actually proves view registration, which the 302 test alone cannot.
- **Verification discipline**: Task 10 report is honest, reproduces every numeric expectation, and the ledger records rulings openly. No secrets, no forbidden paths, no working-tree surprises.

### Deferred-Minors Triage

| Ledger minor | Triage |
|---|---|
| T1 window bounds 1/1440 not accepted-test | Stay — pydantic `Field(ge/le)` is declarative; rejection tests cover wiring |
| T2 frozen dataclasses with dict/list not hashable | Stay — nothing planned uses them as keys |
| T3 tautological asserts; active-product branch uncovered | Stay — smoke covered the integration path |
| T4 `match="phone number"` broadness | Stay — contract only requires `ValueError` |
| T5 no mapper-config CI test; partial constraint-name coverage | Stay |
| T6 report miscounts; SQL branches by design | Stay — smoke compensates |
| T7 truncation/non-dict source untested; empty-source `LeadSource(extra={})`; router `assert` | **Truncation test: fix with the Critical issue below.** Rest: stay — empty source is DB-normalized to NULL and maps back to `None`; assert is unreachable |
| T8 offline-count ruling | Closed — I reproduced it (3 tables in range, 4 incl. `alembic_version` full) |
| T9 admin discriminator ruling/fix | Closed — implemented well |
| T10 human browser check; Watch 1/2 | Human residual, stays; Watches resolved in smoke |

Nothing else on the deferred list must block merge.

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)

**1. Source-value truncation cap (1024) exceeds `utm_*` column width (255) → HTTP 500 and lost lead.**
- `src/app/presentation/api/v1/schemas.py:16` (`MAX_SOURCE_VALUE_LENGTH = 1024`) and `:54-58` truncate *all* source values to 1024, but `src/app/infrastructure/db/models/order.py:44-48` defines `utm_source/medium/campaign/content/term` as `String(255)` (migration same).
- Verified with two probes: (a) `LeadCreateRequest.model_validate` passes a 300-char `utm_source` and 600-char `utm_content` through **unchanged**; (b) a rolled-back `INSERT ... repeat('x',300)` against the live DB fails with `ERROR: value too long for type character varying(255)`.
- Impact: any `utm_*` value >255 chars (ad-platform tags routinely get long, `page_url`/`referrer` are safe at 1024) raises `DataError` in `add_if_not_recent` → generic handler → 500 `internal_error`, and the lead is never saved. Spec §5.1 explicitly promises «заявку не роняем» with log-warning truncation. The current cap is simply ineffective for 5 of the 7 mapped columns.
- Fix: truncate per target column width (255 for `utm_*`, 1024 for `referrer`/`page_url`/extras) with the same warning, or widen the columns; add the missing test (a >255-char utm value → 201 and stored truncated). Also flagging the **spec tension**: §5.1's blanket 1024 rule contradicts §4.3's 255-wide utm columns — the spec should be amended regardless of which fix is chosen.

#### Important (Should Fix)

**2. Spec §10's "отсев неактивных" (and catalog sorting/filtering) is verified nowhere.**
- `tests/api/test_products.py` uses a fake `ListProducts`, so it only proves pass-through; `list_active()`'s `is_active` filtering (`src/app/infrastructure/db/repositories/product_repository.py:61-79`) and variant filtering/sorting have no executable check at any layer, and the smoke ran with an all-active seed (sort order and id order coincide, so it can't even discriminate the sort).
- Spec §10 explicitly listed this for `test_products.py`; with SQL paths excluded from CI by design, the intended compensation (smoke) doesn't cover it. Cheap fix: extend the final smoke/verification to deactivate one product + one variant via psql/admin, re-hit `GET /api/v1/products`, assert exclusion, then restore; or document it as an accepted risk.

#### Minor (Nice to Have)

**3. Dedup window compared against the application clock** (`lead_repository.py:19`): spec §5.4's sketch uses DB `now() - make_interval(...)`; the implementation uses `datetime.now(UTC) - window` against a DB-defaulted `created_at`. Harmless on the single host today, but app/DB clock skew shrinks the effective window in production. Fix: `Order.created_at >= func.now() - window` (SQLAlchemy binds the `timedelta` as an interval bind param).

**4. Bare `assert` in the route** (`src/app/presentation/api/v1/leads.py:20`) — unreachable and stripped under `-O`; brief-mandated, acknowledged. Prefer explicit 500-safe handling if touched later.

**5. Seed downgrade deletes by mutable `code`** (`alembic/versions/...seed_products.py` downgrade): `code` is editable in `ProductAdmin`, so a renamed seeded product would survive a data downgrade. Trivial impact; note only.

**6. Untested branches at the presentation boundary**: non-dict `source` (422 path exists, `schemas.py:45-46`) and `>1024` truncation have no test; the latter should land with the fix for issue 1.

### Recommendations

- Fix issue 1 with a small `SOURCE_KEY_MAX_LENGTHS` map; it also fixes the deferred T7 test gap and keeps the "never drop a lead" guarantee real.
- Implementation/test quality: consider asserting the compiled SQL of `list_active` (where/order_by clauses) as a cheap CI guard if the smoke doesn't get an inactive-filter step.
- Consider the `source_extra` key-count as future anti-spam (out of scope per §13, noting it because a hostile client can store arbitrarily large JSONB).
- Spec hygiene: amend §5.1's 1024 rule to per-column widths; the plan's offline-count expectation (T8) and "9 commits" brief text were already ruled on correctly.

### Assessment

**Ready to merge?** With fixes

**Reasoning:** The branch is high-quality, well-layered, and unusually faithful to its spec; dedup, migrations, admin, and error contracts are all verified end-to-end. It should not merge while the confirmed source-truncation bug (Critical #1) can turn valid ad-tagged submissions into 500s and lost leads, and the spec-mandated inactive-filter verification (Important #2) is absent — both fixes are small and localized.
</task_result>
</task>

input.prompt:
You are executing the single fix wave for the final whole-branch review of branch feat/lead-api. A full review found one Critical bug and two spec-mandated verification/test gaps. Fix them, verify, and report. This is code work — one commit.

## Context

Monorepo /home/nyikolay/Projects/VitaiWorld; backend in backend/ (Python 3.14, Poetry, FastAPI, mypy strict, ruff line-length 100). Branch feat/lead-api, HEAD = 264aa08. A docker-compose stack is RUNNING (app on :8000, Postgres in service `db`, user/db `vitai`/`vitai`); do not stop or rebuild it — you will use it for a live verification below. Read `backend/compose.yaml` (read-only) if you need service names.

## Critical #1 (must fix): source value truncation cap exceeds column widths

`src/app/presentation/api/v1/schemas.py` currently truncates every source value to `MAX_SOURCE_VALUE_LENGTH = 1024`, but the ORM/migration define `utm_source/utm_medium/utm_campaign/utm_content/utm_term` as `varchar(255)` (`src/app/infrastructure/db/models/order.py`). Any UTM value longer than 255 chars passes validation, then the INSERT raises a DataError → 500 `internal_error` and the lead is lost — contradicting the spec's «заявку не роняем».

Fix (implement exactly this design):
- Define a per-key limit map in `schemas.py`:
  `SOURCE_KEY_MAX_LENGTHS: dict[str, int] = {"utm_source": 255, "utm_medium": 255, "utm_campaign": 255, "utm_content": 255, "utm_term": 255, "referrer": 1024, "page_url": 1024}`.
- Derive `KNOWN_SOURCE_KEYS = frozenset(SOURCE_KEY_MAX_LENGTHS)` (single source of truth; `to_domain_source` keeps working).
- Keep `MAX_SOURCE_VALUE_LENGTH = 1024` as the default limit for unknown (extra) keys.
- In `_clean_source`, truncate each value to `SOURCE_KEY_MAX_LENGTHS.get(key, MAX_SOURCE_VALUE_LENGTH)` instead of the blanket 1024, keeping the existing `logger.warning` behavior (adjust its message so it reports the actual applied limit).

## Tests (add to `tests/api/test_leads.py`, using the existing FakeCreateLead/override helpers and VALID_PAYLOAD):

1. 300-char `utm_source` → 201 and `use_case.calls[0].source.utm_source == "x" * 255` (truncated to the column width).
2. 1100-char unknown key (`gclid`) → 201 and `use_case.calls[0].source.extra["gclid"] == "y" * 1024` (extra keeps the 1024 default).
3. Non-dict `source` (e.g. `{"source": 5}`) → 422 and `details[0]["msg"] == "Некорректный параметр источника"` (closes an untested branch).

## Important #2 (must verify live): inactive filtering and sorting of `GET /api/v1/products`

The `list_active()` SQL (product/variant `is_active` filtering, `(sort_order, id)` ordering) has zero executable coverage. Verify it ONCE against the running stack, with restore, and document exact commands + outputs in your report:

1. `cd /home/nyikolay/Projects/VitaiWorld/backend`
2. Baseline: `curl -s http://localhost:8000/api/v1/products` → 5 products, 9 variants total.
3. `docker compose exec -T db psql -U vitai -d vitai -c "UPDATE products SET is_active = false WHERE id = 5; UPDATE product_variants SET is_active = false WHERE id = 1;"`
4. `curl -s http://localhost:8000/api/v1/products` → product 5 (SET) absent; product 1 has only variant id 2; totals 4 products / 8 variants.
5. Sorting discrimination: `docker compose exec -T db psql -U vitai -d vitai -c "UPDATE products SET sort_order = 99 WHERE id = 1;"`, curl again → BR (id 1) is LAST (sort_order beats id).
6. RESTORE: `docker compose exec -T db psql -U vitai -d vitai -c "UPDATE products SET is_active = true, sort_order = 1 WHERE id = 5 OR id = 1; UPDATE product_variants SET is_active = true WHERE id = 1;"` — then curl once more and confirm the response equals the baseline (5 products, 9 variants, BR first).

This DB manipulation is scoped to this verification; the seed/state must end exactly as it started.

## Gates and constraints

- Work from /home/nyikolay/Projects/VitaiWorld/backend; commands via `poetry run ...`.
- No code comments; no other files touched. NEVER touch/stage/commit: Dockerfile, compose.yaml, .pre-commit-config.yaml, .env, frontend/, root .gitignore.
- Focused run while iterating: `poetry run pytest tests/api/test_leads.py -q`; then full gates once: `poetry run pytest -q`, `poetry run mypy src tests`, `poetry run ruff check .`, `poetry run ruff format --check .`.
- ONE commit, staging ONLY `src/app/presentation/api/v1/schemas.py tests/api/test_leads.py`: `fix(backend): cap source values to target column widths`.
- Do not spawn subagents or a reviewer.

## Report

Write your full report to /home/nyikolay/Projects/VitaiWorld/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-15-lead-api/final-fix-report.md: what you changed; TDD evidence (RED for the new tests before the fix: which assertions failed and why; GREEN after); the live verification transcript (commands + outputs for all 6 steps above); full-gate outputs; files changed; concerns.

Reply with ONLY (under 15 lines): Status; commit (short SHA + subject); one-line test summary; one-line live-verification summary (baseline→deactivated→sorted→restored); concerns; report file path.

<skill_content name="verification-before-completion">
# Skill: verification-before-completion

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

<skill_content name="finishing-a-development-branch">
# Skill: finishing-a-development-branch

# Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

**Core principle:** Verify tests → Detect environment → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

## Step 1: Verify Tests

Run the project's full test suite (`npm test` / `cargo test` / `pytest` / `go test ./...`).

**If tests fail**, report the failures and stop — the menu comes after a green suite:

```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]
```

**If tests pass:** continue to Step 2.

## Step 2: Detect Environment

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
# Capture now, while still inside the workspace — Step 5 changes directory
# before cleanup (Step 6) needs this value
WORKTREE_PATH=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
```

This determines which menu to show and how cleanup works:

| State | Menu | Cleanup |
|-------|------|---------|
| `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (normal repo) | Standard 3 options | No worktree to clean up |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, named branch | Standard 3 options | Provenance-based (see Step 6) |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, detached HEAD | Reduced 2 options (no merge) | Externally managed — leave in place |

## Step 3: Determine Base Branch

The base branch is whatever this work forked from — usually named in the
plan, the conversation, or the branch's upstream. If it is not already
known, ask: "This branch split from <your best guess> - is that correct?"
Confirm before merging: merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo.

## Step 4: Present Options

**Normal repo and named-branch worktree — present exactly these 3 options:**

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

**Detached HEAD — present exactly these 2 options:**

```
Implementation complete. You're on a detached HEAD (externally managed workspace).

1. Push as new branch and create a Pull Request
2. Keep as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

Present the menu exactly as written — concise, with every option coming
from the list above. Discarding the work happens only in response to your
human partner explicitly asking for it (see "If your human partner asks to
discard the work" below). Wait for their answer; the integration decision
is theirs.

## Step 5: Execute Choice

### Option 1: Merge Locally

```bash
# Get main repo root for CWD safety
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"

# Merge first — verify success before removing anything
git checkout <base-branch>
git pull
git merge <feature-branch>

# Verify tests on merged result
<test command>
```

If tests fail on the merged result: stop, leave the worktree and branch in
place, and investigate — nothing has been pushed, so the merge is local
and recoverable.

Once the merged result is green: clean up the worktree (Step 6), then
delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -d <feature-branch>
```

### Option 2: Push and Create PR

```bash
git push -u origin <feature-branch>
# From a detached HEAD, name the new branch on the remote:
# git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch>
```

Then create the pull/merge request against <base-branch> with the forge's
tooling — its CLI if one is available, or the creation URL most forges
print when you push — following the repo's PR template and conventions if
present, and report the URL to your human partner.

Keep the worktree — your human partner iterates on PR feedback there.

### Option 3: Keep As-Is

Report: "Keeping branch <name>. Worktree preserved at <path>."

### If your human partner asks to discard the work

This path exists only as a response to an explicit request to throw the
work away. Confirm first:

```
This will permanently delete:
- Branch <name>
- All commits: <commit-list>
- Worktree at <path>

Type 'discard' to confirm.
```

Wait for that exact confirmation. When it arrives:

```bash
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"
```

Then clean up the worktree (Step 6) and force-delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -D <feature-branch>
```

## Step 6: Cleanup Workspace

**Runs for Option 1 and confirmed discards.** Options 2 and 3 always
preserve the worktree. Both callers have already changed directory to the
main repo root — worktree removal must run from outside the worktree —
and use the `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_COMMON`/`WORKTREE_PATH` values captured in
Step 2, from before that directory change.

**If `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON`:** Normal repo, no worktree to clean up. Done.

**If `WORKTREE_PATH` is under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`:** Superpowers
created this worktree — we own cleanup:

```bash
git worktree remove "$WORKTREE_PATH"
git worktree prune  # Self-healing: clean up any stale registrations
```

**If removal is refused** (`contains modified or untracked files`): the
worktree holds files that exist nowhere else — uncommitted plans, notes,
or scratch work. Never `--force` on your own initiative. Show your human
partner what is at stake and ask:

```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE_PATH" status --porcelain -uall
```

```
Worktree removal refused — these files were never committed:

<file list>

1. Commit them to <branch> before cleanup
2. Move them into <main repo root>
3. Delete them (unrecoverable)

Which?
```

Carry out the choice, then remove the worktree.

**Otherwise:** The host environment owns this workspace — leave it in
place. If your platform provides a workspace-exit tool, use it.

## Quick Reference

| Option | Merge | Push | Keep Worktree | Cleanup Branch |
|--------|-------|------|---------------|----------------|
| 1. Merge locally | yes | - | - | yes |
| 2. Create PR | - | yes | yes | - |
| 3. Keep as-is | - | - | yes | - |
| Discard (explicit request only) | - | - | - | yes (force) |

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Tests passed earlier this session" | Run the suite on the tree you are about to integrate. A green run only proves the tree it ran on. |
| "They obviously want it merged" | Integration is your human partner's decision. Present the menu and wait. |
| "They seem done with this feature — I'll offer to discard it" | The menu is complete as written. Discard happens only when your human partner asks for it in so many words. |
| "'Yeah, get rid of it' counts as confirmation" | Only the typed word `discard` authorizes deletion. |
| "The PR is up, so the worktree is clutter now" | PR feedback gets fixed in that worktree. It stays until the work lands. |
| "This other worktree looks stale — I'll clean it too" | Clean up only worktrees under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`. Everything else belongs to the host. |
| "Removal refused — `--force` is just finishing the cleanup" | The refusal means files exist only in that worktree. `--force` destroys them permanently. Show your human partner and ask. |
| "The merged-result failure is probably flaky" | A failing merged result stops everything. Branch and worktree stay put while you investigate. |
| "The base branch is obviously main" | Confirm the fork point or ask. Merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo. |
| "The push was rejected — force-push will fix it" | A rejected push means the remote moved. Investigate; force-push only on your human partner's explicit request. |
